rb_intro_reunion.npc_text: Well, if it isn't Luke. Long time no see. I figured Old Leo still had you running errands across half the district.

player_choices.text: Missed seeing you around, Roberta. The street looked better with you in it.
It's good seeing you again. I missed this place.
Truth is, I'm short on coin. Any chance you could spare a little?

rb_intro_reunion_flirty.npc_text: That is smoother than I remember. Careful, Luke. Keep talking like that and I might start charging you for it. Go on then, say what you came to say.

rb_intro_reunion_friendly.npc_text: Hm. That's kinder than Driftwatch usually sounds. It's good seeing you in one piece too, Luke. Go on then.

rb_intro_reunion_desperate.npc_text: You pick an honest opening, I'll give you that. Fine. Ten copper, one time only. Don't make a habit of coming to me with your hand out, Luke.

rb_first_meet.npc_text: Tide & Trade, finest goods in Port Kael. First time in my shop?

player_choices.text: Looks like you've got your hands full.

rb_repeat_meet.npc_text: Back again? If you're here to browse, browse. If you're here to talk, be quick about it.

rb_trade_root.npc_text: Business first, then stories. What are you after?

rb_ask_root.npc_text: Ask what you want. I prefer direct customers.

player_choices.text: How is the wall repair going?
How have you been managing all of this alone?
What do you want Tide & Trade to become?
If you still mean to set this place right, I can help you do it properly.

rb_friendly_root.npc_text: Friendly, are we? Keep it brief if there is a line forming.

rb_flirt_root.npc_text: You have already crossed that line with me, Luke. So if you mean to be close, be honest about it.

rb_coerce_root.npc_text: If you're going to start making threats, say it plainly.

player_choices.text: Press her and see if she backs down.

rb_quest_root.npc_text: If this is about work, say so plainly.

player_choices.text: How is the wall repair going?
Tide & Trade is set right. You should see it now.

rb_wall.npc_text: The storm took a chunk out of the east storehouse. I need planks to patch it before the next high tide.

rb_trust_refusal.npc_text: I appreciate the offer, but I do not know you well enough to trust you with my shop's repairs yet. Stick around. Trade a bit. We will see.

rb_help_gate.npc_text: I will pay you for the trouble. I need 10 Wood Planks. Bring me those and I will provide the rest.

rb_give_materials.npc_text: Good work getting these planks. Here, take these nails and a hammer I had lying around. Now go fix it.

rb_materials_check.npc_text: The hole is on the east side. Use the hammer and nails I gave you to patch it up.

rb_quest_complete.npc_text: You did a fine job. The draft is gone. Here is your payment, as promised.

rb_ask_managing_alone.npc_text: Badly, some weeks. Properly, if anyone asks. Since my father died, every leak, every spoiled crate, every customer with a complaint lands on me. You either learn to keep moving or Driftwatch starts picking at you.

player_choices.text: That is a lot to carry by yourself.
Most people would have let the place fall apart by now. You did not.
You make it sound heavier than you ever let anyone see.

rb_ask_managing_alone_empathy.npc_text: It is. But the shutters still open, the ledgers still need balancing, and pity never paid a supplier. So I keep the place standing and keep my face set straight.

rb_ask_managing_alone_admire.npc_text: Falling apart costs money. So does pride. I have had to learn how to afford both, and neither comes cheap in Driftwatch.

rb_ask_managing_alone_intimate.npc_text: There is no profit in letting people see where to press. If the whole street knew how tired I was half the time, they would start treating Tide & Trade like it was already up for carving apart.

rb_ask_shop_future.npc_text: I do not need it grand. I just want it solid. A shop that looks worth entering. One that feels like mine, not like a place I am barely keeping from caving in around me.

player_choices.text: Then let us make it into that.
It already feels like yours. The rest of the street just needs to catch up.
You do not just want it standing. You want to be proud of it.

rb_ask_shop_future_support.npc_text: Careful. Say things like that too easily and I might start believing you mean them. Still... if anyone could help set this place right, it might be you.

rb_ask_shop_future_validate.npc_text: That may be the kindest thing anyone has said about this place in months. I know what it could be. The hard part is making the rest of Driftwatch see it too.

rb_ask_shop_future_proud.npc_text: Yes. I think I do. I am tired of this place looking like a problem I inherited. I want to look at it and feel like it belongs to me, fully, not halfway.

rb_second_quest_skill_gate.npc_text: I mean to set this place right, Luke, not patch another hole. You handled the wall well enough, but rebuilding the shop is different. Come back when you have more real experience with carpentry.

rb_second_quest_offer.npc_text: Then we do it properly. No half-measures, no rushed repairs. I will put together the list, and if you really mean this, you can start with the workbench here in the shop.

player_choices.text: I am in. Put together the list and I will start with the workbench here.

rb_second_quest_offer_accept.npc_text: Good. I will keep the list ready. Use the workbench here in the shop when you are prepared and we will set Tide & Trade right piece by piece.

rb_second_quest_complete.npc_text: I noticed the difference the moment I stepped back and looked at the place. The counter sits right, the displays finally look deliberate, and the whole shop feels... mine again. You did more than patch a problem this time, Luke.

player_choices.text: I wanted to see you look at this place and feel happy again.
You deserved a place worth keeping.

rb_lore_tide_trade1.npc_text: Tide & Trade is one of Driftwatch's oldest shops. It has stood through lean years and storms.

rb_lore_tide_trade2.npc_text: My father ran it for decades. He passed recently. I am still learning to handle everything.

player_choices.text: That is a lot to carry alone.
That makes the shop a weakness, doesn't it?

rb_lore_tide_trade_empathy.npc_text: It is. But if I let that show every time the door opened, the whole street would smell blood.

rb_lore_tide_trade_respect.npc_text: You learn quickly in Driftwatch. Either you stand straight or people start measuring what they can take from you.

rb_lore_tide_trade_pressure.npc_text: Only if I were foolish enough to forget where I am. I am not.

rb_friendly_check_in.npc_text: Some days I feel like I inherited a shop and a storm on the same morning. Still, the shutters open and the ledgers need balancing.

player_choices.text: You are handling it better than most would.

rb_friendly_offer_help.npc_text: Maybe you mean that. Most people only offer help when they want cheaper prices.

player_choices.text: I said it because I meant it.

rb_flirt_direct.npc_text: You have that look again. Go on then. Say it plainly.

player_choices.text: You look better in this shop now that it finally matches you.

rb_flirt_playful.npc_text: You sound like you are about to cause trouble. Mild trouble, I hope.

player_choices.text: Only the kind that makes you smile if you let it.

rb_flirt_sincere.npc_text: That tone usually means you mean to say something honest. Risky habit in Driftwatch.

player_choices.text: I like being here with you. More than I expected to.

rb_flirt_tension.npc_text: You keep stepping closer like you are testing a line.

player_choices.text: Maybe I am seeing how close you will let me get.

rb_friendly_honest.npc_text: You work hard. I can see that much. I would rather say it plainly than dress it up.

rb_friendly_compliment.npc_text: If this is flattery, make it quick. If it is not, say what you mean.

player_choices.text: Tide & Trade is still standing because you keep it standing.

rb_coerce_discount.npc_text: Go on, then. Show me what kind of man you are.

player_choices.text: Careful. I can make this shop a lot less comfortable for you.

rb_friendly_check_in_strong.npc_text: That is kinder than most people bother being. Thank you.

rb_friendly_check_in_weak.npc_text: Maybe. I am still standing, at least.

rb_friendly_check_in_fail.npc_text: Flattery does not patch walls, but I suppose it costs less than timber.

rb_friendly_offer_help_strong.npc_text: Then maybe I judged you too quickly.

rb_friendly_offer_help_weak.npc_text: We will see. Driftwatch is full of promises that do not survive the tide.

rb_friendly_offer_help_fail.npc_text: If you are trying to charm me into a discount, save your breath.

rb_friendly_honest_strong.npc_text: Plain words are rarer than they should be. I can respect that.

rb_friendly_honest_weak.npc_text: At least you did not waste my time dressing it up.

rb_friendly_honest_fail.npc_text: Blunt is not the same as sincere, Luke.

rb_friendly_compliment_strong.npc_text: That sounded almost thoughtful. I will give you that.

rb_friendly_compliment_weak.npc_text: Hm. I have heard worse attempts at flattery.

rb_friendly_compliment_fail.npc_text: If you are trying to sweeten me up, you should be subtler about it.

rb_flirt_direct_strong.npc_text: That was dangerously well said. Keep talking like that and I may start expecting it.

rb_flirt_direct_weak.npc_text: Smooth enough. You nearly got away with that one.

rb_flirt_direct_fail.npc_text: If you are going to flatter me, at least make it less obvious you practiced first.

rb_flirt_playful_strong.npc_text: There it is. I was wondering how long it would take before you tried to be charming on purpose.

rb_flirt_playful_weak.npc_text: You are getting bold. Not gracefully bold, but bold.

rb_flirt_playful_fail.npc_text: You really should know by now when to stop one line earlier.

rb_flirt_sincere_strong.npc_text: That... was more honest than I expected. Do not say things like that unless you mean them.

rb_flirt_sincere_weak.npc_text: You make that sound almost dangerous. Honest words have a way of lingering.

rb_flirt_sincere_fail.npc_text: No. If you are going to try sincerity, do not do it halfway.

rb_flirt_tension_strong.npc_text: And what if I let you? You would have to do something with that courage then.

rb_flirt_tension_weak.npc_text: Maybe do not test the line too hard, Luke. Not unless you plan to keep your nerve.

rb_flirt_tension_fail.npc_text: That sounded much steadier before it left your mouth.

rb_coerce_discount_strong.npc_text: Get out of my face. Fine. Take what little satisfaction you came for and leave me be.

rb_coerce_discount_weak.npc_text: That tone might work on someone softer. Don't mistake caution for weakness.

rb_coerce_discount_fail.npc_text: Try bullying me again and you can get out of my shop.

player_choices.text: How do I get planks again?

1.npc_text: Cut logs in the woods, then use the sawmill to make planks. I'll brace the wall once you have them.

rb_give_materials.npc_text: Good work getting these planks. Here, take these nails and a hammer I have lying around. Now go fix it.

rb_materials_check.npc_text: The hole is on the east side. Use the hammer and nails I gave you to patch it up.

rb_quest_complete.npc_text: You did a fine job! The draft is gone. Here's your payment, as promised.

rb_lore_tide_trade1.npc_text: Tide & Trade is one of Driftwatch's oldest shops. It's stood through lean years and storms.

rb_lore_tide_trade2.npc_text: My father ran it for decades. He passed recently. I'm still learning to handle everything.

0.npc_text: The patch held through the last squall. I could not have done it without you.

tide_trade_lore.npc_text: This shop has been in my family for generations. We have weathered worse storms than this.
